title: Esports: Competitive Video Gaming
summary: How organized competitive video gaming trains players in strategy, fast reflexes, and teamwork, and how esports tournaments bring the best teams together to compete for a prize.
poll: Esports is just as much a real sport as soccer or basketball.

versions.title: Esports: A New Kind of Sport
versions.text:
Do you like to play games to win? Lots of kids do. This kind of play is called esports.

Some games are just for fun. Esports games are to win. A team may have a few players. It can take years to get good!

Each player has a job. Some plan the moves. They think what to do in the game. A player must act fast and sure. Some watch for small chances. A chance can help the team win.

Some use fast reflexes. They react fast to what they see, hear, and feel.

First, the team learns the game. It is new. It may feel hard. Kids play it. They see what works and what does not. Then the team talks about it.

Next, the team starts to practice. Then they play it a lot. They look for a skill to fix. A skill can be weak. It can make the team lose! They work on each skill they find.

At last, the team is ready. Kids can join a tournament. But the team still learns new skills and tries new plans.

Lots of kids in Saudi Arabia now play esports, too!

versions.title: Esports: A New Kind of Sport
versions.text:
Do you like to play video games to win? Lots of kids do. But have you ever asked how esports really works?

Some players just play for fun. Serious esports players want to win every match. A team may have a few skilled players. It can take years to become really good!

Each player on the team has a job. Some plan the moves. They choose what the team must do to win. A player needs a fast reflex to act at just the right second. Some players call out the plan. The plan is a set of steps that tells the team what to do.

Others watch for the other team's moves. They watch for patterns, mistakes, and chances to score.

First, the team learns the game well. It is very new to them. It may feel strange at first. Then players try it. They say what works and what does not. The team talks about the game.

Next, the team begins to practice hard. Then they play it again and again. They look for a weak skill. A weak skill can hurt the team. It can make the team lose! They fix each weak skill they find.

At last, the team feels ready, and players can join a tournament. But the team still builds new skills and tries new plans.

Lots of kids in Saudi Arabia now play esports, too!

At last, the team feels ready. But the team still practices and learns new skills.

Today, many young people in Saudi Arabia are joining esports tournaments, too!

versions.title: Esports: Gaming Becomes a Sport
versions.text:
Millions of people around the world watch esports every day. A match may look simple on the screen, but winning one can be a huge challenge.

Some players compete alone just for practice. Top teams, however, need real cooperation. A team may have several members, and it can take several years to compete at the highest level.

Each team member has a special job. Team captains plan the strategy, the goals, and the moves. Players control their characters and read the match, often reacting within a second. In-game callers give instructions, which are a set of signals that tell the team what to do. Coaches study replays and plan drills.

Most teams rely on careful coordination. Coordination means every player moves and reacts at the right time, together. This saves the team from making costly mistakes.

The first step is to build endurance, a steady ability to focus for a long match. It might take weeks of daily drills instead of real matches. Then players scrimmage and get feedback about what is working and what is confusing. The team uses the feedback to make changes.

Next, the team must qualify for a tournament. Coaches review clips again and again to find errors, which are small mistakes in strategy. A mistake might let the other team win a round! Coaches help the team fix each error.

Even after a team qualifies, the team keeps practicing and adding new strategies.

In Saudi Arabia, more and more young people are now learning to compete in esports.

versions.title: Esports: A Genuine Sport of Skill
versions.text:
Esports has grown into a genuine global sport, and although casual players simply enjoy a match for fun, professional competitors train with the same dedication as traditional athletes. Success at the highest level depends on far more than natural talent alone.

Most esports players compete as part of an organized team, not as lone individuals chasing personal glory. Modern esports teams must collaborate constantly, since no single player can carry an entire match alone, no matter how talented that player might be. Teammates study each other's habits, share information during a game, and adjust their plans the instant something unexpected happens on the screen.

Coaches help players optimize every part of their performance, from reaction speed to decision-making under pressure. A coach might design a drill specifically to sharpen one weak area until it slowly becomes a genuine strength. Over months of steady practice, a player's reflexes and judgment both improve together.

Precision matters just as much as raw speed. A single mistimed move, made even a fraction of a second too early or too late, can cost a team an entire match that took weeks of careful practice to prepare for. This is why top teams rehearse the same situations again and again until their timing feels automatic.

Before reaching a major tournament, a team typically must qualify through a series of smaller regional events held throughout the year. Many of these tournaments are funded by a corporate sponsor, whose support pays for prize money, equipment, travel, and the arena itself.

On the day of a major final, thousands of spectators often fill a large arena, cheering loudly for their favorite team, while millions more watch online from their homes around the world, including a growing number of excited fans right here in Saudi Arabia. For these players, the roar of the crowd feels every bit as real as it does for an athlete on a football field.

MID.prompt: Explain why both strategy and teamwork are important for an esports team to succeed, using details from the article.

MID.modelAnswer: Strategy is important because it is the careful plan a team makes and adjusts before and during a match, so they know what to do when something unexpected happens. Teamwork is important because teammates must coordinate their movements and decisions so everyone works toward the same goal at the same time. Without a good strategy and strong teamwork, a team could not qualify for or succeed in a major tournament.

HIGH.prompt: The article explains that esports players must collaborate and optimize their skills to succeed. Explain why both collaboration and precision matter in esports, using at least two examples from the article.
checklist: I explained what collaboration means in this context.
I used at least two examples from the article.
HIGH.modelAnswer: Collaboration matters in esports because teammates must work closely together, coordinating their movements and decisions so that everyone works toward the same goal at the same moment; without this, a team's plan would fall apart during a fast-moving match. Precision matters because even a tiny delay or a slightly mistimed action, such as reacting a fraction of a second too late, can cost a hard-fought match. For example, players optimize their reaction time through repeated drills, and teams review recordings with their coach specifically to find and correct small, precise mistakes. Together, collaboration and precision are what let a team perform as one unit under pressure.
